In [[mathematics]], particular in [[abstract algebra]] and [[algebraic K-theory]], the '''stable range''' of a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] <math>R</math> is the smallest [[integer]] <math>n</math> such that whenever <math>v_0,v_1,...,v_n</math> in <math>R</math> generate the unit ideal (they form a [[unimodular row]]), there exist some <math>t_1,...,t_n</math>in <math>R</math> such that the elements <math>v_i - v_0t_i</math> for <math>1\le i \le n</math> also generate the unit ideal.

If <math>R</math> is a commutative [[Noetherian ring]] of [[Krull dimension]] <math>d</math> , then the stable range of <math>R</math> is at most <math>d+1</math> (a theorem of Bass).

==Bass stable range==
The '''Bass stable range condition''' <math>SR_m</math> refers to precisely the same notion, but for historical reasons it is indexed differently: a ring <math>R</math> satisfies <math>SR_m</math> if for any <math>v_1,...,v_m</math> in <math>R</math> generating the unit ideal there exist <math>t_2,...,t_m</math> in <math>R</math> such that <math>v_i - v_1t_i</math> for <math>2\le i \le m</math> generate the unit ideal.

Comparing with the above definition, a ring with stable range <math>n</math> satisfies <math>SR_{n+1}</math>. In particular, Bass's theorem states that a commutative Noetherian ring of [[Krull dimension]] <math>d</matH> satisfies <math>SR_{d+2}</math>. (For this reason, one often finds hypotheses phrased as "Suppose that <math>R</math> satisfies Bass's stable range condition <math>SR_{d+2}</math>...")

==Stable range relative to an ideal==
Less commonly, one has the notion of the stable range of an [[ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] <math>I</math> in a ring <math>R</math>.  The stable range of the pair <math>(R,I)</math> is the smallest integer <math>n</math> such that for any elements <math>v_0,...,v_n</math> in <math>R</math> that generate the unit ideal ''and'' satisfy <math>v_n \equiv 1</math> mod <math>I</math> and <math>v_i \equiv 0</math> mod <math>I</math> for <math>0\le i \le n-1</math>, there exist <math>t_1,...,t_n</math> in <math>R</math> such that <math>v_i - v_0t_i</math> for <math>1\le i \le n</math> also generate the unit ideal. As above, in this case we say that <math>(R,I)</math> satisfies the Bass stable range condition <math>SR_{n+1}</math>.

By definition, the stable range of <math>(R,I)</math> is always less than or equal to the stable range of <math>R</math>.
